Albert Einstein did struggle with mathematics during his school years, but he never failed it. In fact, he was quite good at mathematics and showed a keen interest in the subject from an early age.

Einstein's struggles with math were more related to his difficulty in understanding abstract concepts and his need for intuitive explanations. He often relied on visual aids and analogies to make complex mathematical ideas more accessible.

At the Swiss Federal Polytechnic University, where Einstein studied physics, he was required to take advanced mathematics courses, including differential equations and calculus. While he didn't fail any of these classes, he did struggle with some of them, particularly in his early years as a student.

Einstein's math struggles were also related to his work on general relativity, which involved complex mathematical formulations that he needed to develop and refine over time. However, this didn't mean he was unable to excel academically; rather, it meant he had to dedicate extra effort and attention to the subject matter.

In fact, Einstein's math abilities were so impressive that he was able to use his knowledge of mathematics to help him develop and understand complex physical concepts. He would often spend hours working on mathematical problems related to his research, using his intuition and creativity to find innovative solutions.

So, to summarize, Einstein didn't fail math in school; he simply had different learning styles and approaches that required more time and effort to master the subject matter.
